title: Harry Styles’ Brand New Together, Together NYC Setlist: Every Song Played at Tour’s First U.S. Show
summary: Styles brought his latest tour to the States for the first time at New York's Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night (Aug. 25), with a totally rearranged setlist.
contentText:
It’s been a building he’s made his own since the 2018 North American leg of his first-ever solo tour, but never quite like this before. When Harry Styles took the stage at New York’s iconic Madison Square Garden last night, he did so for what would be the first of an unprecedented 30 consecutive shows at the storied venue, taking him all the way through to Halloween — by which point the defending-champion New York Knicks will have already played three home games as part of the 2026-27 NBA regular season.

But of course, to the MSG crowd last night, Harry Styles was a star more than equal to Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns, as the One Direction alum and solo superstar brought his best-selling Together, Together tour to New York in support of his dance-flavored February LP, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. Support for Styles came in the form of DJ-producer Jamie xx, who set the clubby tone for the evening with a mix of solo hits, productions for other artists and classics from his beloved indie-electronic band The xx. Styles and his band joined even Jamie xx during his final song, and took over things from there.

New York is the tour’s first and only stop in the U.S., after having previously stopped in Amsterdam, London, São Paulo and Mexico City for a combined 31 dates across July and August. (After New York, Styles will visit Melbourne and City before calling it a day on the trek — for the time being, at least.) Perhaps due to the unique nature of his visit — and Styles’ history with the Garden — he greeted fans with a completely new song ordering from the setlist he’s been playing on Together, Together to this point, including a handful of longtime fan favorites he’d yet to revisit on this trek, and a tribute to a fallen musical icon.

Find the complete new set list for the first of Styles’ 30 NYC shows below.
